![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Move the custom `no-unused-vars` rule configuration to the end of the configuration array (after `svelte.configs`). In ESLint flat config, rules defined later in the array override those defined earlier. Placing it here risks it being overwritten by the Svelte recommended configuration if that config also defines or modifies this rule.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

This assertion is weak because it only checks that the heading is not the same as the initial value. If `initialModeHeading` is null or empty, the assertion `not.toHaveText('')` might pass for unintended reasons. It is better to assert that the heading matches a specific expected value for the selected mode.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Avoid using conditional logic like `if (await ...isVisible())` in E2E tests. This makes the test non-deterministic and can hide regressions where the input *should* have been visible but wasn't. Instead, ensure the test is in a deterministic state (e.g., by mocking the date as seen in other tests) and assert the presence of the expected elements before interacting with them.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Use Playwright's built-in `clock` API instead of manually overriding `globalThis.Date`. This is more idiomatic, less error-prone, and eliminates the need for `// @ts-ignore` and complex constructor logic. Additionally, this logic is currently duplicated; consider moving it to a `beforeEach` block or a helper function if it's needed across multiple tests.

```typescript
\tawait page.clock.setFixedTime(new Date('2026-01-01T12:00:00.000Z'));
```

The test now relies on the `.mode-card` CSS class and positional `nth(1)` selection. Since the home page already exposes stable `data-testid` values on the mode buttons (`data-testid={`home-mode-${mode.id}`}` in `src/routes/+page.svelte`), prefer selecting the second mode via `getByTestId(/home-mode-/)` (and optionally assert the expected count) to avoid coupling test stability to styling/markup changes.

On the home page, the evidence textarea (`data-testid="home-evidence"`) is always rendered (it isn't mode-dependent), so the comment about some modes lacking evidence input is misleading and the `isVisible()` conditional adds unnecessary waiting/branching. Consider unconditionally filling the textarea (or, if you truly need optional behavior, check `count()`/`isVisible({ timeout: 0 })` to avoid long waits when the element is absent).

The `page.addInitScript` Date-freezing logic is duplicated in two tests. Consider extracting a small helper (e.g., `freezeDate(page, isoString)`) to keep the override consistent and reduce future drift if the mocking implementation needs to change.

`languageOptions.globals` currently combines `globals.browser` and `globals.node` for all files. That will prevent ESLint from catching accidental use of Node-only globals in client/Svelte code (and vice-versa). Consider scoping globals via separate config entries (e.g., browser for `**/*.svelte` / client routes, node for `**/*.{js,ts,mjs,cjs}` scripts/server code) while keeping `globals.es2021` common.

This file mixes single quotes (existing imports) with double quotes in the newly added config (`import globals from "globals";`, string literals in `ignores`, rule keys). Align quoting/formatting with the rest of the file (or run the formatter) to keep the config consistent and reduce noisy diffs going forward.
